summary_paragraph: A man with a history of alcohol abuse, COPD, CAD s/p CABG, and esophageal stricture was admitted for urinary retention, abdominal pain, chest pain, and dysphagia. He presented with an enlarged prostate and acute urinary retention, requiring Foley catheter placement which improved his abdominal discomfort. Initial lactic acidosis resolved with fluids. Chest pain was attributed to esophageal stricture rather than cardiac ischemia, as cardiac enzymes were negative. He underwent esophageal dilation, after which his swallowing improved and chest pain resolved. He was started on tamsulosin and finasteride for prostate management and lansoprazole for acid suppression. The Foley catheter was reinserted after failed voiding trial. He was discharged home with services, advised to abstain from alcohol, and scheduled for follow-up with urology and gastroenterology.
problems: Hypertrophy (benign) of prostate with urinary obstruction and other lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS)
Chronic airway obstruction, not elsewhere classified
Coronary atherosclerosis of unspecified type of vessel, native or graft
Gastric ulcer, unspecified as acute or chronic, without mention of hemorrhage or perforation, without mention of obstruction
